body: Review bounded H5 heavy-core census and support-edge ledger. All sectors complete: T0 179994 labeled/1665 normalized; T1 2578/249; T2 52/13. BC=J partitions neighbour supports; heavy graph degree<=2, high+low common-neighbour pruning and residual empty demand. Exact colour groups120/12/8. No singleton/empty completion or exclusion. Frozen source-pins at private folder; independent recount requested.
resolution: PASS (claude). Independent recount reproduces all three sectors exactly. My script (scratchpad rev2022/h5_core_recount.py) shares no code with core_census.py: it re-derives the heavy-core domain from BC=J / C1=7−t / Ct=5 (heavy vertices = pair supports not inside a triple plus the sector's triples), enumerates edge-by-edge by DFS over all candidate edges (different traversal from the vertex-major subset walk under review) with the constraints stated independently — neighbour weight ≤ 5, deg ≤ 7−|S|, neighbour supports pairwise disjoint, all-pairs common neighbours ≤ 1 in core+highs, high-vs-heavy common ≤ 1, empty demand 2−|S|+w−deg ≥ 0 — and normalizes under colour permutations preserving the triple system (group orders 120 / 12 / 8 recomputed from scratch). Results: T0 179,994 labelled / 1,665 normalized; T1 2,578 / 249; T2 52 / 13 — identical to core-t{0,1,2}.json, and the support-edge ledger histograms (a,b,c) = (#pair–pair, #pair–triple, #triple–triple) agree bin-for-bin in all three sectors (T0 eleven bins 1/2/13/68/238/482/521/268/62/8/2; T1 eleven bins; T2 eight bins). Scope as claimed: a complete bounded census of heavy cores only — no singleton/empty completion, no exclusion, no survivor count; the 761 "feasible" hosts-t0 / host-verification.json artefacts in the same folder are a separate pilot that this review did not cover. Master-table row: "H5 heavy-core census complete: T0 1,665 / T1 249 / T2 13 classes (three-way agreement on counts and ledgers) — no kill".
